utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning to everyone. I see we are almost in full force today. Mr. Wubben, I don't see. Could you call the case, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you Your Honours. Case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want a confirmation from you that you can follow the proceedings in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English translation is receiving the B/C/S translation instead of the original floor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a problem? One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There's a technical problem, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought the transcript had got stuck, but it is rolling now. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning Your Honours and good morning to the Defence. My name is De Fazio. I appear with the Prosecution together with my colleagues, Ms. Richardson, Mr. Doria, and our case manager, Mrs. Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it Mr. Wubben won't be with us the entire week. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, we represent the Defence counsel of Mr. Naser Oric. With us is our legal assistant, Miss Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good morning to the Prosecutor as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you, madam, and good morning to you and your team. Are there any preliminaries before we proceed with the videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the issue that you wanted to be addressed upon, namely the length of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that you're happy if the Prosecution addresses you on that towards the end of the week. We feel that you have more benefit from us addressing you then, because there are a number of matters that we want to clear up and hopefully get a more accurate picture by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Yes you are correct. There is no point in trying to insist on a feedback if you are not yet in a 100 per cent accurate position to give one, but please convey our message to Mr. Wubben that we are desperately anxious to know as soon as soon as possible. So take your time, but do come back, because we need to plan for many reasons, particularly because the term of the two ad litem Judges expires, although there is an automatic extension agreed to already by the Security Council, but that in itself also imposes certain restrictions that we need to respect. On the other hand, also, the point -- the message that I want to convey to you is that -- stick to what is barely necessary. I mean there is no point in trying to prove three times what you can comfortably prove with one witness. This is the position. Of course, it doesn't mean to say that you ought to make presumptions, but as experienced Prosecutors you ought to know whether a point that you are seeking to prove by means of a particular witness is proved with some considerable weight or, whether it is dodgy. So, yes Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's precisely one of the matters that we need to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would imagine so. I mean if you realise that there are points in the indictment that you have proved sufficiently already, I think you have a responsibility not to hammer it in. On the other hand, if there are areas which you know you will never be able to prove beyond reasonable doubt, I think it is the case of letting go. I mean, it's -- the case has progressed enough, according to me, enough -- sufficiently enough to make it clear to the Prosecutor more or less where we are heading. So, now, we have -- you don't have any preliminaries on your --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who will be handling the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Jones, are you familiar with the system, how it works, videolink?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We used it once before with another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you are. I don't think I need to explain to you how it works. So let's proceed. The witness is -- does not enjoy any protective measures to my knowledge. Okay. Her name is Stana Stamenic and let's proceed with her testimony now. Yes. Now we depend entirely on the technical people. Yes, I see the member of the registrar, a representative of the registrar on the screen. Madam, can you hear my voice?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, perfectly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are receiving B/C/S interpretation in the head phones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I ask you, again, to repeat please, confirm whether you are hearing my voice.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, I hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I want to know the report on the position from the three interpreters' booth. Are you in a position to hear the member of the registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's very faint and we can also hear the B/C/S channel coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That I could hear as well. And again I think once we know what the problems are, there are two things to be done. One is to increase the volume of the -- on the microphone set where the witness -- which the witness will be speaking into and, secondly, if we could have blocked, as far as those following the English language, if we could have blocked the B/C/S interpretation because, as I speak, I can still hear -- I don't now. I don't now. So let's start all over again. Isa, please could I ask you once more to confirm for me - and speak into the microphone, please - confirm whether you can hear my voice.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I hear your voice perfectly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is very low. Could you really speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is much better. If we could increase the volume it will be better, but I still hear in the background the B/C/S interpretation. A male voice interpreting. It could be a person present in the room who is interpreting. I am informed that they are working on it, so I take it that a solution will be found. In the meantime, let's proceed. I would like to see the witness so that I can welcome her and also speak to her. Good morning to you, Madam Stamenic. Before I continue, I would like you to confirm to me that what I am saying in English, you are receiving in your own language by way of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam, if at any time you are not receiving interpretation, in other words if there are problems with transmission of interpretation in your own language, please draw the attention of the other persons that are in the room, particularly my registrar, the representative of the registrar, because we will need to address that problem immediately before we can proceed any further. Did I make myself clear? Yes, I would like to know if you have understood what I said, in other words whether you have received interpretation. And whether you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If at any time also you would like a rest, please let me know. We will have a break at about 10.30, which will give you a rest, and then we will proceed and have another break at about 12.30, but in the meantime, in between, if you would like to stop for a few minutes for reasons of your own, do let me know. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. My name is Carmel Agius and I come from the island of Malta. To my right I have Judge Hans Henrik Brydensholt from Denmark, and to the left I have Judge Albin Eser from Germany. Together we form the Trial Chamber in this case, which the Prosecutor has instituted against Naser Oric. You will very shortly start giving your testimony and before we proceed with that, according to our Rules, you are required to enter a solemn declaration to the effect that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The young lady representing our registrar who is in the room with you is going to give you a -- the text of this solemn declaration. Please take it in your hands and read out loud the words contained in that text. That will be your solemn undertaking with us, a solemn undertaking equivalent to an oath in many jurisdictions. Did you follow what I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So could you please proceed with your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truly, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, madam. You can hand back the paper to the registrar or to the registrar. You are first going to be asked questions by an officer from the Prosecution. He will then be followed later on by one of -- the member of the Defence team of Naser Oric. Your responsibility is to give a truthful and full answer to the question that is put to you, but only to the question that is put to you. In other words, please do not try to give more information than you are asked. Please try to answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, madam. Yes. Please, go ahead

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, as you heard from His Honour I would appreciate if you could answer exactly to the questions that have been put to you, and if you could restrict yourself to yes or no, that would be very helpful. Madam Stamenic, is that correct that you have born on the 20th of August, 1975?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Is that correct that in January, 1993, you were about 18 years old?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Is that correct that you are of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Is that correct that in 1993 you were living in a small village of Kusici?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, could you please to the Trial Chamber how big is the village of Kusici? Has it any surrounding hamlets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you give the name of the surrounding hamlets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What were the surrounding hamlets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Markovici, Perici, Otave, Petkovci, Riztici [phoen], Beserovici, and Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. The village of Kusici together with surrounding hamlets, were they part of which municipality? Were they part of the municipality of Srebrenica or any other municipality?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Which municipality, please?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many households were in the village of Kusici? I don't want specific numbers, but if you could say approximately how many households were in the village of Kusici. How many families were living in the village of Kusici?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. And was the village of Kusici entirely a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how far from the village of Kusici was the nearest Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And how far was it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: A kilometre, or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Would you also give the name of the nearest Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Kadrici.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that in 1993 you were about 18 years old. What were you doing at that time? Were you sitting together at your home? Or you were in another place, just before the event, the attacks.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I was at home, with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you have any particular occupation? Were you a student?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: During the school break I went to my mother's place in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mentioned a school break. What was the school break? Was that a holiday?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: It was after the end of the first semester.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And I guess this was the period of the Orthodox Christmas in the Orthodox New Year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, may I assume that you were staying at home with your mother. Can you give the name of your mother.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Milena.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to direct your attention to the events that occurred in January 1993. Do you remember what happened in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Our village was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who attacked your village.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what makes you say that they were Muslim forces. Is that because you heard anything being said? Or is that because of the dressing that they had?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The way they were dressed and also I heard that it was them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this needs -- calls for an explanation, both ways. What was in the dress or clothes that distinguished them from others, and secondly, what did she hear? What does she mean when she says "she heard". I think it needs to be explained. So I leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you heard properly what Your Honour said. Can you explain, more precisely, when you say that you recognised them by the way they were dressing. How were they dressing?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniformed as they had read head bands and I also could distinguish them by the way they spoke. They didn't make a distinction between "c" and "c."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, were you aware, madam, that even Serbian soldiers wore camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically if two soldiers, one Muslim and one Serbian, were both wearing camouflage uniforms, you wouldn't be able to tell the difference between one and the other, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had red head bands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically, therefore, it's not the uniform that distinguished the Muslims from other soldiers, but this red band that -- that they were wearing? Headband.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were they all wearing red headbands or only a few? Or a number of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And again you said that the way they spoke revealed to you their ethnicity because there was one letter that they did not pronounce as -- the same way as others did. What was this letter, please? And could you give us an example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The two"c's", with diacritics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you give me an example of a word that would be pronounced differently by you, being of Serbian ethnicity, and another person from your own region being of Muslim ethnicity. Just give me one word and tell me how you would pronounce it and how they would pronounce it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, the family name Mitrovic. I would say Mitrovic. And they would say Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I mean if you're happy with the explanation, then I can come along, but I am not exactly happy. I haven't ... I haven't really found any difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think we will fairly qualify this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, apart from the way in which the soldiers spoke and the red bands that they had on their heads, was there anything else that made you be sure that they were Muslims? Did you recognise anyone among those soldiers, for example?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: The persons that you said were Muslim soldiers, were they alone? Or together with a person not in uniform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't received a translation. I heard the witness say something, like "some" or something like that, but I haven't received the interpretation. Madam, could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you are referring to civilians or only to soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. The question was precisely the following: Were the soldiers that you saw there accompanied by other people who did not have the appearance of soldiers, I would imagine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes. If you could answer that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So were they accompanied by civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Among those civilians, did you recognise anyone which could be from a Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I haven't heard the answer. I saw the witness nodding, but I did not hear her say yes or no. Witness, madam, could you please answer the question again and speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you say that in January, 1993, there was an attack. Can you, for the record, just for the record, state exactly when Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was that the attack occurred, which day, if you have it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you remember the time also?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: When the attack occurred, were you staying at home or outside your home?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What were you doing outside?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: My mother and I were on our way to the cattle shed to tend to the cattle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you say that an attack occurred, what do you mean? Did you hear anything, something like a -- fighter jets bombing the village, or rifle shots?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Shots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But shots of what? I mean because this is basically what the question was aiming at. Can you distinguish between shots and shots? I mean, the question was whether this was rifle shots or whether there were bombings. First of all let's you go there it one by one. Were there any planes flying at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you exclude categorically the dropping of bombs or rockets from aircraft, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean "no"? In other words there were no attacks from the air, is that correct, there was no attacks from the air?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the attacks were from the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the attack consisted of shots, you said, just shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only shots, shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So no rockets? And no mortars, no mortar firings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Stamenic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: When you heard the first rifle shots, as you're saying, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: My mother and I started running.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Where? You were running where, to which place?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Towards my grandmother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you able to reach your grandmother's house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Where were you injured?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: In the left thigh bone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did your mother help you with the wounding?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: She put me on her back and she dragged me all the way to my grandmother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And did you reach your grandmother's house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Why? What happened?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers caught up with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How many soldiers, do you know?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, from the morning when you heard the first shots, rifle shots, and the wounding and the soldiers captured you, do you recall how much time elapsed between these two phases, from the moment when you hear the first shots until when you were captured, actually captured? Was that a question of seconds? Or minutes? Hours?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you think that the soldiers, the Muslim soldiers were actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps my learned friend might finish the question but I anticipate what he's going to say and I object. It's not for her to speculate as to what the soldiers might -- might not have been doing while she was getting wounded. He is about to call for speculation on her part, it is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour if she knows what was happening or she thinks what might have been happening, I don't see why the question can't be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Doria I would suggest you finish the question because we haven't heard it as yet and then we will decide whether it is the case of accepting your pre-announced objection, or not, Mr. Jones. Could you tell us what your question is, Mr. Doria, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you say that there was a lapse of time of minutes between the moment when you heard the shots, the first rifle shots of the attack and the moment when you were captured, wounded and captured. Do you think that the soldiers were far away from your house or close to the place in which you were wounded and captured? A.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is perfectly legitimate. Which soldiers? The ones --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I mean the ones that captured her, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam, in your opinion -- let me rephrase the question myself. There was a moment when you were shot, followed by you being carried over by your mother a short distance, followed by your capture. In your assessment, were the persons who captured you very near where you were ultimately shot and captured, or did they have to travel quite a distance to capture you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I'm not sure that they were close. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At least do give us an idea of, from the moment you were shot to the moment you were captured, you already said that it was a question of minutes, but would you be able to tell us approximately how many minutes? A few minutes? Two, three minutes? Five minutes? How long did your mother have to walk with you on her back before you were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some four or five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That gives us more or less a good idea of where we are. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, just for record, you say that you were injured. What caused the injury into your thigh bone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut it short. Were you shot? Did you have a bullet wound that fractured your thigh bone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, at the moment when you were shot, were you in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. The soldiers that captured you, where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: You mean where I was captured?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: No. You say that when you were going, running into the direction of your grandmother's house, the soldiers appeared and captured you. Where did they take you, from there?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They took us to our house, the house where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And did you find your house in the same state in which you left it? Just the while, while you were going to the stable?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I could see the stable burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. And when you came back to your house, in which state did you find your house? Was it also burning?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you find anyone else, apart from the soldiers that captured you, around your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you give us numbers, not specifically, but how many were those soldiers there around your house, around your burning house.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Some 20 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnicity were they? Do you think that they were colleagues of those who captured you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you think that they were Muslim soldiers too?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone among them who you knew, who you knew before the war as a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I knew a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Who was this woman?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Djemila.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone else among them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: After you reached your house, was your wounding dressed? Did you get any help from whoever?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Apart from the house which was burning, did you see anything else? Did you see people taking things from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What were they taking from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Blankets, some buckets with cheese.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who were the people taking things from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: They were only civilians? Or also soldiers among them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Some soldiers also went into the house and came out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: When they went into the house and came out of it with things also? You mean they were also taking thing from your house, is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: These questions are being put in a very leading way, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've been showing some restraint but if my learned friend could simply ask her what she saw, what happened, rather than putting words in her mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I hate to interrupt you, but, at the end of the day she has already told us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry about that. Yes. Could you ask less direct questions, Mr. Doria, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: The soldiers you say the soldiers were getting into your house and coming out. Did you see anything? Why were they going into your house and coming out?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: The civilians that you saw going into your house and coming, why were they going into your house and coming out?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, is it really for this witness to speculate about why people are doing things, about their motives? Again she should -- she's said what she's seen, and I think my learned friend should move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's a question of English more than anything else, Mr. Jones. I can't go on doing this myself, can I? One moment. Mr. Doria, can you rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you; I will try Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, earlier you stated that you saw civilians taking blankets and cheese from your house. My question was: Have you seen soldiers also doing the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's a different question and that question has already been put, and she said "no," and she's answered it. She said it was only civilians then later he said, "Did you see anything else?" And she said, "no." And now he was supposed to -- my learned friend was put the previous question in a different way and he has gone back to an old question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness said she saw soldiers getting into her house and coming --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut it short. Madam Stamenic, you've told us that you saw civilians in your house and you saw soldiers in your house. They both came in and went out. Who did you actually see taking things out of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't want to tell you straight away Mr. Jones is right, but I knew he was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, in your statement, you also say that you saw, among the soldiers, a postman, that you recognised as being a Muslim postman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because again we can't go on -- we can't proceed along these lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: May I rephrase the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, of course, you have suggested to the witness what she has already stated in the -- in her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: She was asked whether she recognised anyone else among the civilians, and she said, "no, apart from Djemila," it doesn't seem that she needs to have has her -- her memory refreshed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She can refresh her memory, of course, by reference to her statement. But he has to do that first, in the orthodox, traditional way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, from the moment when you came into your house or you were captured and came into your house, you say that you saw people going around and taking things from your house. Did you notice anything else happening, apart from what was closer to your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You said earlier that you also saw your stable burning, is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else about your stable burning?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that around 6.00 the attack occurred and then thereafter you went to your house. What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: When? When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: When the soldiers captured you, they took you to your house. And then what happened after that? What did they do with you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They put me on an ox cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And then what happened? Did they take you to another place? Or you stayed all the time in front of your house burning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They took me off, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. You were injured. I take it that you were also bleeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was your injury addressed at any time, at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did the soldiers take you to anyone -- anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Which place?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They said they were taking us to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Now, from the time when you were captured until the moment when you were taken in the direction of Srebrenica, do you recall how long -- how much time elapsed in between the two moments? When were you taken to Srebrenica? At what time?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime around noon. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: During the time when you were waiting in front of your house, did you see -- what were the soldiers doing? Were they sitting in front of you looking at you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What were they doing? The soldiers and civilians, were they all there? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers were moving about and so were the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: They were just moving?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They were loading up things from the house, up on to the ox cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Which houses? In whose houses were those?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: They were looting things only from your house or from other places?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them do it from the other houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Madam Stamenic, do you recall them offering you any payment for the things that they loot from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall them giving you a receipt for the things that they took from your house? Or promised that they will pay you later?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, did you ask them to go and take things from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that you were taken to Srebrenica. First of all, who told you that they were -- you were going to be taken to Srebrenica, and for what reasons?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Djemila, the woman told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did she also tell you why you were being taken to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: For an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: So she told you that you were going to be prisoners and being exchanged later, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He didn't say prisoners. Again, my learned friend keeps putting words in her mouth. He can simply ask, "What was said?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection sustained, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Okay, I will rephrase. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can pass to the next question, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, on your way to -- first of all, on your way to Srebrenica, did you see anything happening on your way to Srebrenica? Did you pass across any other Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you see anything happening on your way to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw houses that had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall in which places?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Brezani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Did you see anything else, there and in other places?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Madam Stamenic. When you were taken to Srebrenica, do you recall how you were taken there? Was that that you were walking yourself? Or you were put on a -- on a transportation means?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On the cart or --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness specify whether she means vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you hear the interpreter? I want to make sure Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that you did so that you can phrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you mean that you were not walking by yourself. You were put on a -- was that a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Phrase it differently. What kind of a cart? What kind of a cart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't go on foot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What kind of a cart were you transported in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ox cart. On an ox cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you alone on this cart?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mean that there were no other persons in the cart?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall anything else on that cart? Being put in that cart, carried in that cart? Was it an empty cart?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, there were blankets and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mean the looting was inside the cart, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You don't need to continue, Mr. Jones. You can't use the word "looting" that's for us to decide later on, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you please ask her what happened to her mother in the meantime. Where was her mother?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, what happened to your mother? Was she together with you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when -- because I want to make sure that there is no problem in either interpretation or anything. Earlier on Mr. Doria asked you whether you were alone in the cart and you said, "more than once." Actually, you confirmed that you were alone in the cart. Do you mean to say that your mother was not with you in the cart? Or was she with you in the cart, on the cart, anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, she wasn't sitting with me in the cart. She walked along by the cart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. So that explains it. Yes, Mr. Doria. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, on your way to Srebrenica, who was following you? Was anyone following among those who captured you? Or you were meant -- you were made to go to Srebrenica alone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is confusing, Mr. Doria. One moment. Please be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Maybe I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, were you escorted to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know by whom?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you arrive in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall if, on your way to Srebrenica, you were escorted by the same soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. You say that you arrived in Srebrenica on Sunday. Do you recall which day was that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Was that the same day or the next day? The attack occurred on the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall at what time did you arrive in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: About 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Madam Stamenic, do you recall if, on your way to Srebrenica, anyone else either from your village or other village was together with you? Did you meet anyone else who went together with you to Srebrenica, on your way to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: On all of your way to Srebrenica, you were only you and your mother, the civilians, Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: No, I mean only you and your mother. No one else.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived in Srebrenica, to which place were you taken in Srebrenica? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: To the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And your mother?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: To the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: So your mother was taken to the police and you to the Srebrenica, to the Srebrenica hospital, is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you treated in the -- at the hospital, Srebrenica hospital?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Anything else happened while you were staying at Srebrenica hospital?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: A soldier hit me with his -- kicked me with his foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Why he would do that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, next to me there was a dead soldier lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Now, when he kicked you, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He swore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems that there is a technical problem, because we cannot hear the voice of the witness. We don't hear the witness's answer, and we haven't been for three minutes now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. I wouldn't be able to guess that. So thank you for pointing that out, Madam Vidovic. The technicians have heard you. So let's proceed and see whether the problem still exists, or whether it is solved or can be solved. And if it is not solved, then we obviously have to stop until it is solved, because you have every right to hear her answers in your own language. So, Madam, you were telling us that you were taken to the hospital in Srebrenica and that while you were there you were hit or kicked by a soldier, and that you were lying next to a dead soldier, and -- when this happened. And that when he kicked you this other soldier swore. I think -- do you confirm this, to start with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I heard her, so I take it that you have heard her as well? All right. I'm not going to ask you any further questions myself on this. It's up to you, Mr. Doria, to see whether it is the case of elaborating a little bit or whether to move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you say that the soldier swore to you, what do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, he used bad language. He said that I had been carrying a rifle and that I had killed that soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not swearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, could you give an explanation to the contradiction between what you said earlier and the -- using the word "swearing" and later saying that actually the soldier accused you of being, carrying a rifle and killing the soldier next to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, he swore. He used some words. I don't remember the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move to the next question, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You said that you were treated at the hospital. What kind of treatment did you get in the hospital, at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: My wound was cleaned and dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who did that to you, who cleaned your -- your -- and dressed your wounding? Was this a doctor? A nurse?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: A nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, after being dressed, after your wound was dressed, where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: To the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: So you went back to the police station?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: When you went back to the police station -- when you came to the hospital and went back to the police station, do you recall if you were alone or someone else following you or company escorting you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Escorted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who was escorting you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if they were the same soldiers that took you -- captured you in the village of Kusici and took you to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you mean these were the same soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you said earlier that in the cart in which you were put that there were also some blankets and some other things there. Do you recall -- can you recall if those things were still there?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. You were taken to -- back to the police station and what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They took my mother out of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you taken also into the police station, inside the police station?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Okay. You met your mother outside the police station. And what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They took us off up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: They took you to where? First of all, when you say "they took us," who you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mean the same soldiers that were escorting you all the time?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: THE INTERPRETER: There was no sound coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you repeat your question, please, Mr. Doria, because there is a technical problem with the sound, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You were referring to "they took us" and I wanted to know, Madam Stamenic, whether this "they", you said the soldiers, were the same soldiers that were escorting you all the time from Kusici until Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have a break perhaps at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Stamenic, we are going to have a 25-minute break now and we will come back soon after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The accused is here. Again, I wish to draw your attention to the interpretation. If there are any problems at any time, please tell us straight away so that we address those, address them straight away. Yes, Mr. Doria, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, just for the record, could you state, again, your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Stana Stamenic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Again for the record, could you state the full name of your mother, please.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Milena Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how old was she at the time of the events in 1993?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: She was in her 40s.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, I would like to take you back to the events in January, 1993, specifically at the time when the attacks started again. You testified having seen civilians together with the soldiers in front of your house. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And you also testified having seen those civilians going into your house and taking blankets. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall seeing those civilians taking other items, apart from blankets, from your house?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Could you, Madam Stamenic, describe a picture of what was happening for the Trial Chamber, please. What were the items?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Buckets with cheese.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Any other items? Please give a picture, a general picture of what was happening.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: So you just saw them taking blankets and cans of cheese, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm just wondering how many times my learned friend is going to ask this question. She answered very clearly twice and the last question any other items and she said "no," and if he keeps putting this question it's going to be clear to the witness he wants her to mention other items. In my submission she has given at least clear answers to this question and my learned friend should move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Doria, perhaps you can ask the third and final, for the third and final time whether there was anything else and leave it at that and proceed to your next question immediately after, please, if you have a confirmation that there was nothing else being taken out of the residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, I would please ask you to be -- you may speak calmly and freely and give a picture of what was happening to the Trial Chamber. That would be very helpful. Thank you. Again, have you seen any other items being taken from your house, apart from those that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you said that those civilians were taking things from your house. Do you know which ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, do you recall having given a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in May 2000?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall having read that statement?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall having agreed to that statement?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour if I may be allowed to refresh the memory of the witness on one particular point in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, two points, really, Your Honour. Firstly think the witness should be asked whether she thinks it would assist her to see her prior statement, because without that there is no need to refresh her memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We also need to see whether she has it available.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's the second point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I imagined you would raise that. Let's clear this last point first and foremost. I would like to know whether the copy of the witness's alleged statement is available to her in the room where she is giving testimony now. Well it's -- I need an answer either from the witness herself or from the registrar representative.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have a copy of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I took it that they don't have a copy. Is that correct? Because I heard "nema, nema," so what I suggest is that if you are going to refresh the witness's memory with regard to particular issues, then you read no read slowly because the interpreters have to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is what I wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, without the witness actually seeing her signature, or purported signature on the statement without being able to follow in Bosnian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's a question of cross-examination later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, how does she know those are her words?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I'm saying this is ultimately a question of cross-examination. At this point in time I can assure you I'm not going to put any questions myself, especially since the statement is not there. And that's ... It's Mr. Doria's problem, actually. Neither yours nor ours at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But it's simply to note that the witness is going to have to take Mr. Doria's word for it, that this is what is recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, if she is prepared to do it. This is why I'm saying, actually, it is Mr. Doria's problem and not really yours or ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria. One moment. One moment. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Doria. You may refresh the witness's memory by reference to what you allege to be her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, finally, could he simply ask the witness if she thinks it would help to refresh her memory to see her statement because it may be she has a perfectly clear recollection and doesn't feel it would assist her at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That is a perfectly valid point, too. Perhaps you could start with putting that question first to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just proceed along these lines. Ask her whether you are right in submitting that she made a statement or that she was interviewed and her statement allegedly reduced in writing, whether she had signed that statement, the date of that statement, and whether she would like parts of that statement read out to her to refresh her memory, particularly in areas where you think she needs her memory to be refreshed. I'm not saying that that is the case, but this is the order in which you need to proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you remember having signed the statement that you read?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, I would like to refresh your memory on one particular point from that statement. Do you think that that would be helpful for you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, in that statement, you mentioned, in particular, the following: "When I was brought near my house that was burning, there were about 100 soldiers in total. Out of them I identified the local postman, Ismet, and a Muslim woman who was a friend of my family by the name of Djemila." Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Stamenic, do you know if the postman was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if the postman was -- how was he dressed, the postman?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: In civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if apart from the postman there were other civilians?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Male civilians, too?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if those civilians -- do you know the ethnicity of those civilians?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you testified that in the village of Kusici, and the surrounding hamlets, there were a number of households. Do you remember if, at the time of the attack, there were other Serb villagers [Realtime transcript read in error "villages"] in that village?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I agree. The transcript, it is neither your fault, Mr. Doria, nor the witness, actually. It's -- neither your fault nor the witness, but we need to clear this because as it is the transcript says, reports your question as being "do you remember if, at the time of the attack, there were other Serb villages in that village". So I suggest that you rephrase or repeat your question and then the witness would be asked to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you remember if, during the attack, there were other people, other Serbs in that village, apart from you and your mom?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you know if those Serb villagers, which were together with you, were also taken -- captured by the Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Have you seen any other Serb villagers being captured at that time, that day?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you state -- testified that you saw your stable burning. Do you know if you had any animals in that stable?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You don't know if, in your stable, you had any animals?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I think, to clarify that. I mean really the follow up question should have been: "Is it that you don't know there weren't any animals in the stable." And still -- from the next answer it's still unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, were there animals in the stable?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were two cows, but that was before the stable was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to those cows thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I saw them in the meadow over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you have any other animals apart from the cows?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber which were those animals?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you testified that in the cart on which you were taken to Srebrenica, there were put some items, like blankets and some other items. Do you know if the soldiers, the Muslim soldiers also were putting those items into the cart?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Firstly, I think she only mentioned blankets. I would have to check whether she mentioned some other items. But secondly it is a very leading question. He should -- she should simply be asked does she know where the blankets came from or something of that nature rather than suggesting to her that soldiers were loading up the carts with blankets, which is obviously where he wants to get to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She did mention buckets of cheese.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Being taken from her house, but not necessarily on the cart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. But that's because you said you want to check something. I mean, she did mention buckets of cheese. I don't recall her mentioning anything else that I can remember, but ... Anyway, you got the point, Mr. Doria?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I got the point and I will try to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you testified that you saw blankets and buckets of cheese being taken out of your house. You also testified that you saw those items in the cart that took you to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I saw blankets, but I don't know whether those were the same ones that had been taken out of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who put those blankets into your cart?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you said that together with the soldiers were civilians, and that the soldiers escorted you to Srebrenica. Do you know if those civilians also escorted you to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She answered this question before, because you had asked her a specific question on this. Let's move, Mr. Doria, because we are repeating. I'm going through a phase which I thought we had already passed, but anyway, let's proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you know if those civilians were carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Madam Stamenic. Madam Stamenic, you say that when you came -- when you arrived in Srebrenica, your mother was taken to a police station. How do you know that it was a police station?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: That is what it said on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you also testified that at the hospital a soldier kicked you. Do you know which ethnicity was that soldier who kicked you at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you testified that the soldier, when he kicked you, he told you something like: You have killed the Muslim which was lying close to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I mean, I hate to interrupt you, Mr. Doria and it's not my style to do so. But this question was put to her already and she has answered the question so it is not a case of refreshing her memory. She has also told us where -- who was lying dead next to her, and what -- that this other man swore at her, and accused her of -- she has already stated all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. She also said nothing about Muslim soldier. She said "dead soldier."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question was what was the ethnicity of the dead soldier, what was the ethnicity of the other person -- soldier that kicked her, that is perfectly legitimate at this stage, but not other questions because we have already covered those. Otherwise we will be here with this witness for the next two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I might make a brief observation on that -- that point. I need an hour and a half with this witness, and at this rate she will have to come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's -- she is -- I don't -- again, it's not our problem, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. But one other point on that, is that clearly my learned friend is trying to get her to accept that the soldier was Muslim by reference to a dead soldier being a Muslim and, in my submission, that is inappropriate. She said she doesn't know the ethnicity and he should move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is as inappropriate as you put it, Mr. Jones. But, Mr. Doria, please go straight to the point, put the questions you need to put without repeating aspects of the events that we have already covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to make sure that it was clear for the Trial Chamber because earlier the witness testified that when she was kicked and the person said that he kicked the Muslim [sic] close to her, and now when I ask her about the ethnicity, she said she didn't know what the ethnicity was of that soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ask her about the ethnicity, but don't try to rub it in. We are following what the witness is saying. I mean we are not asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, let's move on to the next question. Madam Stamenic, you say that when you arrived back to the police station, you met your mother there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You also testified that soldiers escorted you from there to another place. And I asked you if those were the same soldiers who were escorting you from the village of Kusici until Srebrenica. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She has already confirmed it, Mr. Doria. I mean, she -- if you go back to your transcript you will find the same question and the answer that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour I will move to the next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we should move to see what was her state -- how her state at the police station could be described, who was there, and move forward, because otherwise we are going backwards instead of forwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, did you notice anything at the police station?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I mean, anything such as what? What do you mean to ask the question to the witness? And are you referring to how many windows there were? Whether it was clean? Whether it was not clean? Who was there? What they were doing? What was -- where was ... Just go straight to the point. I mean after all, what is relevant to the case is what happened there. And who was responsible, if at all, to what happened there. I mean, the rest is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, let's move. Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you say you met at the police station your mother much. Then you were taken somewhere. Can you tell the Trial Chamber to which place you were taken.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: We were taken to the prison where we spent three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you say that you were taken to the prison, can you describe what was this? Do you mean that it was a private house, or it was a public building? Or something else?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were bars on the windows.
