utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. Were you taken to a room in that -- in that building?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if that prison that you are saying, was -- was it close to the police station? Where was it? Do you know where was it located?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't spend too much time getting there from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find anyone else in the room in which you were put?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. The persons that you found in the room in where you were put, were they males or women?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Women.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you aware of any male prisoners in that building?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not then, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mean the male prisoners were not in the same room in which you were?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Let me rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, could you clarify your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There weren't any men, just women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It doesn't need clarification, if she tells you there were no men, there were no men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you know if there were any male prisoners generally in the building? Not in the room in which you were put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You put this question already. If you look at line 7, of page -- on page 47, where were you aware of any male prisoners in that building. The answer was "not then, no." Then, "You mean the male prisoners were not in the same room in which you were?" And then there was the objection. Then was, "Let me rephrase." Okay. Fine. "Could you clarify your answer." "There weren't any men, just women." So it doesn't need ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour I think that she has in mind the room in which she was, that's why I want to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you say that there were -- madam, when you say that there were "no men," "no males,", do you mean to say in the room where you and your mother were being kept? Or in the entire building of the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They weren't in the room where my mother and I were kept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in the rest of the building, were you aware of the presence of males? I saw her say "da," but I didn't hear her say "da." Can you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know then when they brought us there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when did you find out that there were male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Over the next few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Madam Stamenic, I would like you to give a picture of the room in which you were placed. Do you know how many women were together with you in that room?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were several.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you give any specific numbers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give any names?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, could you describe the room in which you were put.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were two windows with bars on them. The door was metal. There was a big bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, do you know if the women that were in the cell in which you were put, were they of which ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnicity were they? Were they Muslim or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how did they appear? Do you know how did they appear like, were they like --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop there because I anticipate my learned friend is going to suggest how they might have appeared. Why don't we just let the witness answer how they appeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Also let Mr. Doria finish his question too. Let's hear your question first before we authorise the witness to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how they appeared like, Madam Stamenic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again it's a question that can be answered in various ways. It depends on what --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: That's why I want to make the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But then put a more specific question, without it being a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, can you comment on what sort of women were they? Were they local prison women or ... How was their physical appearance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one. First of all, who was with you in the cell, let's take this series of questions one after the other. Who was with you in the cell? Or in this room where you were being kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was my mother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there was Dostana, Andja, and another woman from Kravica, I don't remember her name, then there was Zivana and her daughter and a small boy. His name was Branko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, do you know the ethnicity of each an every one of these persons who were with you in this room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were they all of the same ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what was that ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were all Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Apart from your mother, did you know any of them from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So how can you explain to us how you came to know that -- or how you can confirm that they were all of Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They told me their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So are you telling us that they were Serbian, of Serbian ethnicity because of the Serbian names that they had? Or was there any other reason for you confirming that they were of Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of their names, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were dressed in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what was their general condition of health?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Back to you, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Stamenic. Thank you, Your Honour; thank you, Madam Stamenic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you give a further picture of the conditions inside the women's cell. You say that you were brought to Srebrenica on the 17th of January, 1993. Was it cold at that time?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you have any sort of heating in the room in which you were placed?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What sort of heating you had in the cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a wood stove, a wood-burning stove.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you mean a stove used with firewood?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How often did you get firewood, and who brought it to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: We didn't get it often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who used to bring the firewood to you, in those period in which you got them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you explain better, please, to the Trial Chamber. Who used to bring the firewood to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, it was brought by a man whom I knew; his name was Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know his family name?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Ivanovic? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall anyone else coming to bring you the firewood?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Two other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come back to those males later. Did you have any blankets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if the other women also had blankets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Later on they were brought blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how many?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if -- well, let's put it another way. Where were you sleeping during your time in the room?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And do you know where was sleeping the other women in the cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On the bench, roundabout.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if they had -- do you know if all the women were on that bench, how big was the bench? You said there were around ten women in the cell.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And where we're all of those women, ten women, sleeping on that bench?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No. They couldn't fit on the bench, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: So where were they sleeping, the others who couldn't fit on that bench?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: My mother was next to me, my stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you mean on the floor close to your stretcher, is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you have any other bedding, apart from the -- like mattress or pillows or whatever?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, can you recall if you ever were fed during your stay in that cell? Did you get food and water?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How often did you get food? What sort of food you get?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Once a day. Sometimes soup, or a thicker soup, or a small piece of bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How big was the piece of bread, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, like an ordinary box of cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you given enough water to drink?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They brought us water in a bottle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Was that enough for you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: It depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, do you know if there was any toilet close to your cell or in your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not in the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Across.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you ever taken there?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, both -- the women, but not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Where did you relieve yourself?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There was a bucket in the corner and that's where.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were the other women allowed to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, when they would let them go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How often were they allowed to go?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Maybe in the morning and the evening, but rarely. Infrequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Was it possible for them to go in other periods of time when they needed it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you say that "when they were allowed to go," who do you mean by "when they allowed them to go"? Who was allowing them to go?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The guards at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who were the guards?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnicity were the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat whether she said yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam, could you repeat your answer, please, because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you know if the guards, that you're saying the guards, were in uniform? Or in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know the colour of these uniform?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if the uniform, the camouflage uniform, was the same as the one of those soldiers who escorted you to Srebrenica? Was that of the same sort?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I mean, was it also of the same sort of the camouflage uniforms that the Serb soldiers used to wear? Could you distinguish between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our soldiers wore green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But when they -- you also told me earlier on that sometimes they wore camouflage uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And would there be a difference between the camouflage uniforms that the Serbian soldiers would wear and the camouflage uniforms that these people that were guarding the room were wearing? Or would the camouflage uniforms be exactly the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police wore blue, blue uniforms. But in a pattern, like camouflage. Whereas the other ones were green camouflage and these were blue camouflage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Stamenic. Madam Stamenic, did the guards mistreat the women in the cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did they threaten them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did the guards ever enter the women's cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. They would bring in water.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: At the time when they would come and bring the water, that was the only time when they would enter your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Apart from the guards, do you know if any other soldiers would come into the women's cell?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He just -- soldiers, they're guards not soldier.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly; you can't use the word soldiers in your question, Mr. Doria. Use any other word -- apart from these guards, would anyone else enter the room? Did anyone else enter the room in which you were being kept?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Madam Stamenic, you heard the question of His Honour. Did anyone else, apart from those guards, enter your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us who, please, if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A nurse came to dress my wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the nurse who came to dress your wound, anyone else came --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's also important -- one moment. I'm sorry to interrupt you with -- if that is the case, a nurse came to dress her wounds, how often this happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once while I was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And how long after your arrival in the prison did this nurse come to dress your wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A week, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you -- was this in response to your specific asking for a nurse to dress your wound? Or was it done without you asking for attention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't ask for it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Apart from the nurse who came in your cell and the guards, did anyone else come to your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were these persons in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if she knows who they are first and then you ask the question of what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who were those persons who came into your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who were they?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There was a man, he introduced himself as being called Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He came and asked whether anybody was perhaps mistreating us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And what did you answer to him?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: We said we weren't being mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: This is Zulfo. Did he come in daylight or at night, in the evening?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if he was able to see that you were lying on that stretcher, wounded?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did he offer help to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from Zulfo, did you see anyone else coming into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. This visit by this man who described himself as being Zulfo occur before the nurse came to dress your wounds or after, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you describe how this Zulfo looked like?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How tall he was?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not very tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Was he in civilian clothes or military?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before you move. What was his age, most likely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Middle aged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you remember if he was big? Round? Did he have a moustache?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He was a bit tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Anyone else came into your cell, apart from Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Another man came and he introduced himself as Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What did he say else, apart from introducing himself?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He asked us if we received any food.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: We told him how much we got.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Could you describe this person who presented himself as Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He was a somewhat younger man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. And was this person who presented himself as Naser Oric able to see you in that stretcher wounded?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The question was put that way last time as well. I wasn't very comfortable it. Surely the question is if she was in this -- on this stretcher at the time, which presumably she was, and then one can draw one's own conclusions as to what he saw because she doesn't know what -- or any other person sees or notices. It's a small point, but I think it needs to be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I perfectly agree with you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Could this person who presented himself as Naser Oric, able to see you on that stretcher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've put it exactly in the same way. When this person who according to you presented himself -- introduced himself as Naser Oric came into your room, where were you at the time? Were you lying on your stretcher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware whether -- if he saw you there or not? Do you know if he saw you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Back to you, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. He approached me and asked me why I was on this stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And what did you answer?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I told him I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What was his reaction?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Doria, perhaps you could ask the witness whether, in relation to the visit by the nurse, whether this visit by the man she says introduced himself as Naser Oric, whether this was before or after the visit of the nurse or by the nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall when this person, who presented himself as Naser Oric, came into your cell, from the time when you were put in the cell.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did this person, who presented himself as Naser Oric, offer you any help?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if he came before or after the nurse?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from the three persons that you mentioned, was there anyone else who came into your cell, that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: One man came and pointed his pistol at my head. I don't remember who he was or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He just cursed and swore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How did you feel when that happened?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did he do the same thing with other women in the cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. During your custody during the three weeks that you were in custody, were you scared at all?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you scared when anyone came into your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Afterwards, were you or others taken outside for interrogations?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Other women were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know who did interrogate them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know how often they were taken outside for interrogations?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: From time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if your mother also was taken outside for interrogations?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if those interrogations happened in day light or in the evening, at night?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know, do you remember if you had any lighting in the night?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You didn't have a light, or you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if the persons that you just mentioned, were the only ones who came into your cell during all the three weeks, or were there other persons coming and threatening you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Only these people came.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for the record, the way the question was put might imply that the persons who came threatened her. There was one person, obviously, who threatened her and it shouldn't be implied that any of the others did, the nurse or this person called Zulfo or the person who introduced himself as Naser Oric, just so that is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your point is well taken. I mean I think the problem is linguistic more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't mind that, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So perhaps you can rephrase your question. I mean, it's no big deal, but I think it is better if you rephrase your question because ultimately the -- these transcripts will have to be read and there is no guarantee that it will be just us who will read them, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Apart from the man who you say -- you testified that came and threatened you with a pistol, do you recall anyone else coming and doing the same thing to other women, the same?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you earlier referred to certain Ilija Ivanovic and some other two males who came and brought to you firewood. How did they look like?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Bent. They were bent over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know why they were bent over?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you say that sometime later when -- after you were brought to the women's cell, you came to know that there were male prisoners, males held in the same building. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know where was the location of this room in which the males were held?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps she can tell us how she came to know that there were, after all, males in the buildings. How did you come -- you put the question, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes. You hear His Honour asking. Madam Stamenic, if you could describe us better the situation. How come you to know that there were males in that building, I understand, apart from the guards?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I heard screams during the night and wailing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: All right. How often could you hear the screams?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I saw the witness saying something, but I am sure that whatever she said could not be heard. So if she could perhaps repeat her question -- her answer, and I think she -- there is some problem also in that the way she spoke seems to indicate that there is some problem with your -- with hearing your question to start with, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, how often did you hear the screaming? You say that you heard screaming. How often did you hear the screaming?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Twice a night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know if you heard the same screaming during daylight too?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you heard these voices, do you know if the voices that you were hearing was something, like, close to your cell? Or very far away from your cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Close to my cell. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you mentioned one male coming into your room with the name of Ilija and some two others. Do you know if those males were coming from that cell?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't know about those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, when you say that you heard voices during the night, at least twice at night, screaming, what do you mean by "screaming"? Was that -- was it in the sense of crying out of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't put any leading questions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: What do you mean by "screaming"? Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: What I meant was that they were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Could you hear any other noise, apart from the human voice that you hear screaming?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I heard something like a bat, somebody being beaten by a bat or a pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the sounds of the bat and the voices of those screaming, did you hear any other voices at that time?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard people shouting "Get up. Get up."

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there was screaming. Can you explain better what kind of screaming was that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: You know when a person is moaning or wailing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, I know. You already said it was out of pain. Is that what you want to say again?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You say that you heard the sound of bats. How often did you hear this sound?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how often I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that you stayed in prison for a period of three weeks. What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Then we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How did you come to know about the exchange? Was there anyone?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Zulfo came and told us that we would be exchanged the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You mean the same person who presented himself as Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And when did he tell you about that? Was that -- I mean from the time when he told you about that and the time when the actual exchange took place, you were?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: One day before we were to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. You earlier also named two persons, you say the one was Ilija Ivanovic and some other two males who came with the wood. Do you -- do you remember their ethnicity? You said you knew him?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I only knew Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And which ethnicity was Ilija?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you know which ethnicity were the other two who came in to bring firewood for you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Stamenic. During your time in the women's cell, did you ever -- were you able to wash yourself? Were you taken to a lavatory or a shower?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, again, if you could -- if you can recall, the three males who came into your cell, could you notice anything from their physical appearance? You said earlier they were bending. Did you notice anything else on them?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that one day before you were exchanged a person who called -- a person Zulfo came in and announced that you were going to be exchanged. Do you recall who took you from the cell to where -- how that happened, could you describe to the Trial Chamber, please. I mean the next day when the actual exchange took place.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: My mother was there and two women took hold of her, each -- on their sides, and that's how they took her out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you escorted by anyone?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Who was escorting you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, if we could have a break, I think it's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So madam, we are going to have another break, 25 minutes again, and we will continue soon after an hopefully finish with your examination-in-chief. The understanding is, Mr. Jones, that you will then start with your cross-examination, either immediately upon termination of the in-chief or tomorrow. There's no way we can finish with this witness today, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. That is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can proceed. Yes, Mr. Doria, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you testified that during your custody in prison as someone who presented himself as Naser Oric came in to the women's cell. Do you remember if that person identified himself also either --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I wonder if again it's going to be a leading question with a suggestion as to what else he said. Why doesn't my learned friend ask if anything else was said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. I am afraid I have the same suspicion -- thank you, Mr. Jones. Mr. Doria, I have the same suspicions as Mr. Jones, actually. I don't know what your question is going to be but you may make it sound as if you're going to put words in the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I will try not to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fine. We would greatly appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall what was he wearing? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No audible response

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree, I saw the witness making gestures with her head but we could not hear her answer. Could you please repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall him identifying himself either by position or rank?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: He said he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you say that eventually you were released from your captivity. Do you recall when was that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The 6th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: On that day you were released from the prison, and were taken where?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I was taken for an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you were escorted, or not?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall who escorted you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall which uniform did they have?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I mean, do you recall -- do you recall the colour of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall how you went to the place of the exchange? Was it by a car, by a -- or any other vehicle?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Another vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Which one was that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Like a combi van.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall any other women being exchanged with you, being released from the prison?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall numbers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, on the 6th -- you say on the 6th you were released. Do you recall the place in which you were taken from the detention, from the prison?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber where was it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Between Kraglijivoda and Jezero.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, do you recall who was -- who was the person in charge of the exchange, on the part of the Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, from the moment that you eventually -- do you remember what time did you come to -- did you arrive in the place of exchange?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: We set off from the prison sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And when did you arrive?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: About an hour or two later. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall for whom were you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, they took out the dead from the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were they Muslims? Or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Do you recall to whom were you handed over during the exchange?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Who were the persons to whom you were handed?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Well, I remember the man. His name was Cubus ^, that's how they referred to him anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Where is this -- the persons were they civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were they Muslim or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, after the exchange, where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: To Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: To your home?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No. I was taken to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in hospital after the exchange?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: About three-and-a-half to four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Were you able to be treated properly?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Was it in Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, thank you very much for your testimony. Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Jones, shall we start now?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think I can make use of the time since we have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we have more than half an hour, with the understanding that you stop when it is most convenient for you, so it's up to you. The other thing I wanted to make clear is that we will obviously finish quite early in the day tomorrow. So I would like to know, here and now, if you will be able to bring forward C002 tomorrow to start his or her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour we believe at this time period, since the proofing session is continuing, we have contacted Mr. Di Fazio to find out whether it would be possible to go forward. I've been informed that the preference would be, if the witness would start on Wednesday morning and not tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But that's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I please try to return to you prior to the end of this session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. Please do. Because ... Anyway, that's the least said the better. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, Miss Stamenic, just to start I'm going to ask you some questions about your village and the general area. Now, firstly, Kusici is a hamlet in Zabornica village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's also near Kostolomci, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Kostolomci is a little further away, across the hill, over the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But it's a matter of a few kilometres, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, in fact, just for the benefit of us more than anything else, I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to suggest it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I do have copies of a map which I will pass up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. We do have a map here, but it's not easy to follow unless someone indicates the various spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. This map is of the Skelani area, which is being passed up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other thing I want to make sure is that if this map is put on the ELMO, for the benefit of the witness, I want to make sure that the witness can actually see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think that won't be necessary for the moment. I just wanted to establish those two places, Kostolomci which we see roughly in the middle of the map, and then further down Zabornica further down and to the left, and then Skelani there, again, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Stamenic, in 1992 and early 1993, wasn't your hamlet guarded by men in the village?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know Stanoje Mitrovic and Slavko Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: They were part of that guard, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now I take it you saw them around the village. Isn't it correct that they were wearing olive-green JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They wore green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Those of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. The standard type of army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And didn't they also have a Papovka, semi-automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know who issued them with those rifles?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Aside from those soldiers, isn't it right that the Serb army, the army proper, had its front lines above your hamlet, Kusici, on the hill?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it right that that line was established at the start of the war, so around April/May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, we are having problems in spotting Kusici on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately it doesn't appear there. It might assist if I ask the witness about some other villages, and to see whether those are close to her village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: For example, Ms. Stamenic, is Pavkovici near your hamlet? Pavkovici.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is Malta, the village, near your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: It's Djabokvica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You've told us that Kalmanici was near your hamlet. How about Dvizovici, is that also near? Dvizovici.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would it be right to say that your hamlet is somewhere between Dvizovici and Kalmanici?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, do you know where Popovici is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Savici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [ Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How -- is Savici far from your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you know where Drmnik ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And again, is that far from your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's further off than Savici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. So am I right in suggesting that your village was somewhere between Dvizovici and Savici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, over the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. You see, it's a good thing to be able to read maps, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm obliged Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, in fact, in perhaps, finally, Okalardi [phoen], is that anywhere near your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not too far off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can stop there. We have an idea now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that a Muslim village, Kaborici [phoen], was one or two kilometres away from your hamlet. Resagici was also nearby, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Resagici, further away, closer to Skelani, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But you knew some of the Muslims from Resagici from before the war, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And didn't you also know a number of Muslims from Dobrak, another Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Because in fact you went to school in Skelani, didn't you, and you knew many Muslims from the area from your schooling?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Regarding these Muslims in your area, in Dobrak, Resagici and other places like Tihici, Ragovici [phoen], you got on well with your Muslim neighbours, didn't you? You had coffee with them, helped them out with chores, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you mentioned a Muslim woman named Djemila, she was actually a friend of your family before the war, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Where -- where was she from, if you could help us with that?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: She was from Dobrak.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But when we turn to January 1993, when you saw her, she wasn't living in Dobrak at that point, was she?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, isn't it true that at that time the hundreds of Muslims from that area, from Dobrak, Aragovici [phoen] had all left their homes?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you have any idea why the Muslims left their homes, their farms, their fields, and everything they had worked for?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it something that you ever asked about or enquired about or tried to find out about?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you accept that possibly they might have been forced to leave by Serb soldiers and paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may have I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I don't think the witness could have known why and under which circumstances. I think it is speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's speculation, obviously it will be ignored, like every other speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is nothing to suggest that she may have the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. right answer for that question based on her actual knowledge of the events at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. She could have learned about that in a hundred different ways. She could have seen it, she could have heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I know that you are on cross-examination, not on examination-in-chief. I think I will -- definitely I have no doubt at all that we should allow the question and, if it is speculation obviously we will ignore it and remind or draw the attention of the witness not to speculate. Which I am doing now in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I will put the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you aware, Miss Stamenic, that the Muslims in your area had been forced to leave their homes by soldiers, paramilitaries and locals?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You're not aware of that? You're -- you're stating categorically that that did not happen?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Turning to the events of 16th January, 1993, you told us how you were wounded in the left thigh during the attack. Just before you were wounded there were in fact shots being fired all over the place, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you didn't see who shot you, did you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you don't know whether the person or persons who shot you were the same as those who captured you, do you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And isn't it right that as far as you know you could have been shot by a stray bullet rather than by someone deliberately targetting you? The fact is you don't know one way or the other, do you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe it was a stray bullet. I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you've spoken about how your hamlet was attacked by what you referred to as the Muslim army and you've also spoken at length about soldiers. So I want to break that down a bit. Now, firstly, you knew nothing at the time, did you, of how any Muslim armed forces were organised, if indeed they were organised?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: At the time -- and possibly later, you don't know if there was one Muslim army or many Muslim armies?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nor did you know whether the fighters who you saw were in any way organised as any modern army would be; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I didn't know whether they were organised or not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So would it be correct to say that when you referred to the Muslim army, you're essentially referring to a collection of fighters whom you believed to be Muslim?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, as far as soldiers are concerned, on the 16th of January 1993, you saw men and women all mixed up together, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of January?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. In other words, men and women were all mixed up together. There weren't separate groupings. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, starting with the men, isn't it right that some men wore some kind of uniform and others were in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as far as any uniforms were concerned, isn't it true that there wasn't one standard uniform that you saw? There were different colours and different styles?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms with red bands.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. But that just applies to some of the men you saw, correct? You're not -- you're not saying that everyone you saw was wearing camouflage uniform and red bands?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Those that I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're doing exactly what you criticized Mr. Doria for doing. She had already given you a straightforward answer and you tried to get a different answer from her.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, no. Your Honour it's -- there is a matter which needs to be clarified, which hopefully my next question will make clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- which is the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it right that there were men who wore either a uniform or part of a uniform but who didn't have red bands, whom you saw?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I saw them with the bands.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, as far as the bands are concerned, are you quite clear these were red bands tied around the head, and not black arm bands tied around the arm?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Red bands around their foreheads.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So you didn't see any black bands or ribbons tied around the arms of any of these fighters?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as far as the men you saw on that day are concerned, many of them had no weapons at all, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this needs a little bit of clarification. She didn't see, what?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you saying that you didn't see a single uniformed fighter without a weapon?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I couldn't see if every single soldier had weapons of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact that there were tens if not hundreds of people in the area around your -- the hamlet and village that day?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And leaving the men aside, you told us there were women there as well. Were there children as well who you saw?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And old people?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just finally then on the matter of soldiers, would it be correct to say that when you refer to "soldiers," you're referring to men with weapons and with these red bands, firstly?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But you have no idea which army or forces they belonged to, assuming they belonged to any forces?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. "No," in that you have no idea to which forces, if any, they belonged? I think I have the answer. I will move on to another question. Now the people who captured you on that day, didn't they in fact treat you perfectly properly, in fact they brought a stretcher out for you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And isn't it in fact also the case that Djemila took you into her house and changed your clothes, because they were bloody?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Her and my mother went into the house. They found a room that was still not on fire and they found a skirt there. They brought out a skirt and they took off my trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So your mother and Djemila, the Muslim lady, went into a burning house to get dressing to attend to your wound?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I wonder if it could be clarified which house they are talking about. Is it Djemila's house or the witness's house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you put your question yourself, Mr. Jones, otherwise I will put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I can with the proviso that, of course, if the Prosecution think there are matters, they can raise it in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which house was it that was on fire, partially on fire?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as far as your house is concerned, you didn't see anyone actually set it on fire, did you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nor did you see anyone set fire to your stable?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And while we're on that subject, you told us how on the way to Srebrenica you saw burning houses I think it was in Brezani, again you didn't see anyone set those houses on fire, did you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I saw that those houses had already burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So to summarize, you don't have any idea, do you, who, if anyone set fire to any of the houses which you saw burning or burnt?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, going back to the help which Djemila and your mother gave to you, after you'd been wounded, would you agree that they, first of all, did all they could to help to reduce your discomfort?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And would you agree that that is also true of the other Muslim fighters and civilians who were in the area at that time, that to the extent that they did anything, they helped you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that they took you to the hospital in Srebrenica for treatment?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you told us that Djemila was a local Muslim woman, Djemila, who announced that you would be taken to Srebrenica to be exchanged. Did you understand from this, that that was how the Muslims would get back their live people or their dead, by taking you to Srebrenica and then exchanging you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: At that moment I did not understand anything. I didn't know -- I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But that's eventually what happened, wasn't it, you were exchanged for dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you a little bit about the sight which you had of objects being taken from your house. Isn't it right that they were mostly taking food, these civilians, from your home, namely cheese?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were they grabbing the food pretty frantically, and even fighting each other over the food; is that something you saw?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you get the impression, from what you saw, that these Muslim civilians were desperately hungry?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: They may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you also mentioned how blankets were taken. It's right, isn't it, it was very cold at this time?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I think I have a few more questions on one subject and then we can wrap up for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is entirely up to you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, the journey to Srebrenica which you undertook by cart, took a very long time in fact, didn't it? It took nearly a whole day.

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the cart was travelling at roughly walking pace, was it?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was an ox-driven cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So that's roughly, then, how long it would take to walk to Srebrenica from Kusici, nearly a whole day?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Not the whole day, as we took a longer road.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know why you took a longer road?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, upon arrival in Srebrenica, you were taken immediately to the hospital, weren't you? You weren't taken to a police station and asked questions or anything?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: The hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. My point was this: You were taken straight to the hospital, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Straight to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, finally, if you can help us with this. As you arrived in Srebrenica, on the road going into Srebrenica, did you not see the sight of hundreds of people out on the streets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: There were people. I don't remember how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But many people?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: They were in a fairly wretched state, were they not, living out on the streets?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, did you have the opportunity to observe their appearance and see whether they looked starving and sickly?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, you didn't notice? Or they looked in perfect health to you?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you see them burning fires outside for warmth and to cook food?

utterances.speaker: STANA STAMENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think we can stop there for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones, and I thank you Madam Stamenic. We will meet again tomorrow morning and hopefully we will finish with your testimony within a relatively short time. I thank you once more. You will be attended to by our staff over there and we will make sure that you will receive all of the attention you -- and the assistance you need. I thank you. Yes, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In terms of tomorrow's witness, I understand the witness is currently on a lunch break. What I suggest is that I will contact the legal officer and Defence this afternoon after being able to ascertain whether the Prosecution can go forward with the witness's testimony, or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. As far as we are concerned, although I haven't had the time to consult with the other two Judges, but if what I am saying is not agreeable, please speak out. Is that from the amended witness list that you yourself -- when I say "you" it's not you, understandably -- the Prosecution has submitted C-002 was scheduled to start tomorrow and not on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this witness that we will be finishing tomorrow was scheduled to start today and finish tomorrow, and indeed she is going to finish tomorrow, but then we had also scheduled that C-002 will start tomorrow. So to shift that will require pretty much convincing, let me tell you straightforward already. We will not really like to waste the rest of the day tomorrow. Half an hour here or there won't make a difference, but I'm trying to stress the point that we ought to start with C-002 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I clearly understand what you're saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 2 is, we will be moving to courtroom 1 tomorrow. The sitting is still in the morning, but not in courtroom 2, but in courtroom 1. The other thing I wanted to alert you to is that because of certain family exigencies of one of the members of the Trial Chamber, we will not be sitting on the 22nd of April. So you are scheduled to start a witness on the 22nd of April, I won't mention his or her name because I am not sure if he or she enjoys protective measures, but that witness can still -- can start on the 21st if you finish the previous witness on the 21st, but please be advised that we will not sit on the 22nd. And we are trying to do our level best to make some adjustments to the sitting of the 28th, moving it from where it is, but I thought we had been successful. We haven't. There has been a roundabout turn, and for the time being, the schedule for the 28th remains as it is. In other words -- but we are trying to change that, to shift it to the morning. So we meet again tomorrow morning. I take it that you will finish by the first break? It's up to you. If it's not possible, we will ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That would really seem about right, another hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems so ... Yes, thank you, Judge Eser. Mrs. Stamenic, before I let you go, I don't know where you are and I don't know who is with you, but I want to make sure that between today and tomorrow you do not allow anyone to approach you to discuss with you the things that we are discussing here and that, from your part, you also not discuss any of the subject matter of your testimony with anyone. I know that I can count on your word. I just want you to promise me that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
